subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's 1989 run is psychedelic superhero storytelling at its most surreal and adventurous — Dadaist villains, deeply weird concepts, and a genuine compassion for outsiders. Rachel Pollack continued well; later volumes include Gerard Way's acclaimed Young Animal relaunch.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Fraction's long run is the modern Iron Man benchmark — Tony Stark fighting Ezekiel Stane, losing his mind, and rebuilding. David Marquez's clean art in later issues is exceptional.
author: Matt Fraction

subject: series
synopsis: Tie-in to the animated series — arguably better than most of its contemporaries. Adam Beechen and Dwayne McDuffie's contributions especially are sharp, well-characterized superhero stories.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Spin-off anthology from the Archie Sonic comics. Ian Flynn's stories expand the lore effectively; best enjoyed by readers already invested in the Archie Sonic mythology.
author: Ian Flynn

subject: series
synopsis: Tie-in to the beloved Hanna-Barbera animated series. Earnest, wholesome superhero comics for young readers from the 70s and 80s.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2018 relaunch of MAD from Burbank, soon turned largely into a reprint magazine of classic material.

subject: series
synopsis: Bryan Hill and Stefano Caselli's 2024 Ultimate Universe Black Panther: T'Challa leads Wakanda against the avatars of Khonshu and Ra.

subject: series
synopsis: Kosuke Fujishima's long-running manga about a goddess accidentally summoned to live with a college student. Gentle romantic comedy with charming world-building; at its best warm and sweet without being saccharine.
author: Kosuke Fujishima

subject: series
synopsis: Collected volumes of Matt Wagner's noir mystery series following the 1930s Sandman Wesley Dodds.
author: Matt Wagner

subject: series
synopsis: Acclaim/Valiant's 1993 Turok: the time-lost Native American warrior battles dinosaurs, aliens and Mothergod in the Lost Land.

subject: series
synopsis: Bill Mantlo and Michael Golden's adaptation of the Mego toy line is one of the finest licensed comics ever produced — richer, stranger, and more emotionally resonant than any toy tie-in had a right to be.
author: Bill Mantlo

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's 1988 Animal Man: Buddy Baker's animal-rights crusades turn metafictional until he meets his writer, followed by Milligan, Veitch and Delano.

subject: series
synopsis: A collected volume of the New 52 Green Lantern: New Guardians series featuring Kyle Rayner and his team battling the god-killing threat that has decimated powerful cosmic beings.
author: Justin Jordan

subject: series
synopsis: Yoshihiro Togashi's manga is one of the most intellectually ambitious shonen works — the Yorknew City and Chimera Ant arcs are masterpieces of tension, character, and thematic density. Chronic hiatus pains don't diminish the achievement.
author: Yoshihiro Togashi

subject: series
synopsis: Louise Simonson and June Brigman's beloved series about four young siblings who gain superpowers and fight crime as the Power Pack -- Marvel's first ongoing series starring an all-child superhero team. Charming, all-ages adventure with strong family dynamics.
author: Louise Simonson

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's groundbreaking She-Hulk series, the first mainstream superhero comic to systematically break the fourth wall. Jennifer Walters talked directly to readers, complained about her own comic, and engaged with the medium's conventions in a way that was funny, self-aware, and genuinely inventive.
author: John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen's space opera: Samandahl Rey, a soldier of the Planetary Union, gains the Sigil mark and fights the reptilian Saurian empire.

subject: series
synopsis: Stephanie Phillips' 2024 Spider-Gwen: The Ghost-Spider: Gwen Stacy back on Earth-65 amid the Spider-Society and the Spider-Verse.

subject: series
synopsis: Dwayne McDuffie's Milestone hero — a Black teenage superhero from Dakota City powered by a mutagenic 'big bang.' One of the most culturally specific and authentic superhero origin stories in mainstream comics.
author: Dwayne McDuffie

subject: series
synopsis: Yoshiaki Sukeno's supernatural action manga about two teenage exorcists destined to produce the prophesied Miko who will end evil. Dramatic escalation with strong central relationship.
author: Yoshiaki Sukeno

subject: series
synopsis: Frank Tieri and Georges Jeanty's 2002 Weapon X: a revived program under Malcolm Colcord recruits mutants like Sabretooth and Agent Zero.
author: Christina Z., Frank Tieri

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's oversized magazine-format anthology that ran from 1977-1986, featuring adaptations of films (Star Wars, Raiders of the Lost Ark, Alien), rock bands (Kiss, Beatles), and original stories in an impressive oversized format.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel reprint anthology from the 70s. Archival value — collecting early Avengers stories that were otherwise out of print.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2013 digital-first Superman anthology: out-of-continuity stories by rotating creators.

subject: series
synopsis: Green Lantern renamed for the Corps (1986-1988): Steve Englehart and Joe Staton's team of Lanterns on Earth with Hal, John Stewart, Arisia and Kilowog.
author: Steve Englehart, Joey Cavalieri

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel anthology featuring Ka-Zar and Doctor Doom, then Deathlok. Notable primarily for the Deathlok stories by Rich Buckler.
author: Gary Friedrich

subject: series
synopsis: CRC Payne's webcomic series collected for DC — wholesome slice-of-life about the entire Bat-family living together. Enormously popular for its warm characterization and humor.
author: CRC Payne

subject: series
synopsis: Daniel Clowes's essential anthology series containing Ghost World, David Boring, and Ice Haven — among the most influential works in literary comics, mixing suburban alienation with dark humor and formal experimentation.
author: Daniel Clowes

subject: series
synopsis: DC horror anthology from the 70s. Typical of the era's anthology horror with rotating framing characters. Solid genre material.

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' critical magazine covering the comics industry and art form; the most serious and important critical publication in American comics history, home to landmark interviews with Crumb, Spiegelman, Eisner, and many others.
author: Gary Groth

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek and Mark Bagley's 1997 Thunderbolts — the Masters of Evil posing as heroes, unmasked in a celebrated twist — then Fabian Nicieza's long run.
author: Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: Amazing Spider-Man volume 2 (1999-2003): Mackie and Byrne's relaunch, then J. Michael Straczynski and John Romita Jr.'s run from #30.

subject: series
synopsis: Naoki Urasawa's thriller manga is one of the greatest mystery narratives in any medium. A group of childhood friends realize their imaginary villain plan is being enacted for real by a cult. Intricate, rewarding, and emotionally devastating.
author: Naoki Urasawa

subject: series
synopsis: Cassandra Cain's 2000-2006 Batgirl: Kelley Puckett and Damion Scott's near-silent assassin's daughter learning to speak and atone, later Horrocks and Gabrych.

subject: series
synopsis: John Francis Moore and Pat Broderick's 1993 Doom 2099: a Doom awakened in 2099 retakes Latveria and later seizes America; Warren Ellis's closing run.

subject: series
synopsis: Haruichi Furudate's volleyball manga transcends its sports genre to become a profound meditation on effort, teamwork, and finding your place. Beautifully executed with an enormous cast, each member distinctly developed.
author: Haruichi Furudate

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's early 2000s X-Men reinvention is radical and brilliant — Weapon Plus, Quentin Quire's mutant riot, Planet X, and the discovery of Weapon X. Frank Quitely's art defines the era. One of the most important X-Men runs.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Rick Remender's run is one of Marvel's finest — a black-ops X-team that kills when necessary, grappling with the moral weight of that decision. Wolverine, Psylocke, Deadpool, Archangel, and Fantomex form one of the best team rosters in recent memory.
author: Rick Remender

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1970 split book — Kirby's Inhumans and the Black Widow, the Beast's furry turn, then Don McGregor and P. Craig Russell's Killraven.

subject: series
synopsis: Roger Stern and Tom Lyle's 1988 Starman: Will Payton gains cosmic powers in a satellite accident, a light superhero series of 45 issues.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Chris Bachalo's 2013 Uncanny X-Men: Cyclops's outlaw revolutionaries train new mutants after Avengers vs. X-Men.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Gold Key and Whitman's 1975 Looney Tunes anthology: Bugs, Daffy, Porky and friends in short gag stories.

subject: series
synopsis: Alyssa Wong's delightful spin-off starring the variant Loki who is a small alligator. Wordless visual comedy that is unexpectedly charming and emotionally resonant.
author: Alyssa Wong

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's 1976 weekly launching Brian Braddock as Captain Britain, by Chris Claremont and Gary Friedrich with Herb Trimpe, alongside US reprints.
author: Chris Claremont, Jim Steranko

subject: series
synopsis: Reprints of Claremont's Uncanny X-Men with new backup stories adding extra character texture. The backup stories are surprisingly rich — essential for Claremont X-Men completists.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Earth 2 series — a parallel Earth where Golden Age heroes exist as the primary heroes. Tom Taylor's Earth 2: World's End is the peak of this particular corner of the DC universe.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: The official webcomic tie-in to the NBC television series Heroes, providing backstory and expanded universe content for characters like Hiro Nakamura, Claire Bennet, and Peter Petrelli. Primarily for fans of the show.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Barbara Kesel's CrossGen fantasy about a young woman who inherits a mark of power on a world of floating islands. One of CrossGen's stronger titles — adventure with genuine emotional stakes.
author: Barbara Kesel

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen series about Giselle Villard, an arrogant socialite who becomes a magic user in a steampunk world. G. Willow Wilson's recent Marvel revival is the better version.

subject: series
synopsis: Chuya Koyama's manga about two brothers pursuing their dream of becoming astronauts is one of the most human stories in manga — a realistic portrayal of adult ambition, failure, and perseverance.
author: Chūya Koyama

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan's 2022 Invincible Iron Man: a broke Tony Stark battles Feilong and marries Emma Frost amid the Krakoa era.

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 1993 Bloodshot: framed mobster Angelo Mortalli, turned nanite-powered killer by Project Rising Spirit, hunts for his stolen memories.

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander and Tom Mandrake's 1992 Spectre: Jim Corrigan's wrathful spirit wrestles with justice, sin and God's purpose.
author: John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Jessica Drew's first series (1978-1983): Marv Wolfman, Mark Gruenwald and Chris Claremont's moody, supernatural-tinged run.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Saladin Ahmed and Aaron Kuder's 2023 Daredevil relaunch, following Chip Zdarsky's run.

subject: series
synopsis: Oversized collected editions of the acclaimed noir sci-fi series about genetically engineered animal-human hybrids.
author: Richard Starkings

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Davis's lasagna-loving cat strip is one of the most successful comic properties in history. The early years have genuine wit; the strip has coasted on brand recognition for decades.
author: Jim Davis

subject: series
synopsis: A DC anthology series spotlighting members of the Justice Society of America in self-contained arcs, including a notable opening story exploring Power Girl's contested origins. A showcase for the DC Universe's first super-team.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Timely Comics' golden-age anthology — one of the first Marvel (then Timely) comics. Human Torch and Namor both appeared here. Essential golden age history.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Ron Marz's CrossGen fantasy series. A crown prince caught between warring kingdoms and branded with mysterious power. Competent fantasy adventure.
author: Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel anthology that launched Ghost Rider, Son of Satan, Moon Knight, and Spider-Woman — an extraordinary incubator for new characters in the early 70s.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Brad Meltzer and Ed Benes' 2006 Justice League of America relaunch after Identity Crisis, followed by Dwayne McDuffie and James Robinson.

subject: series
synopsis: Larry Hama's Marvel G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero (1982-1986): the Joe team versus Cobra, including the wordless #21.

subject: series
synopsis: Batman's 2007 covert Outsiders team under Chuck Dixon, then Peter Tomasi; our files also hold Mike W. Barr's 1983 original.
author: Chuck Dixon, Frank Tieri

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Williamson and Sean Izaakse's 2023 Green Arrow: Oliver Queen lost in time while the Arrow family searches for him, extended into an ongoing.

subject: series
synopsis: Simon Spurrier and Mike Deodato Jr.'s 2023 The Flash: Wally West confronts strange cosmic hungers in the Speed Force in a cerebral run.

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Tomasi's digital-first tie-in to Rocksteady's Arkham Knight video game. Solid companion material for fans of the game; less essential for general readers.
author: Peter Tomasi

subject: series
synopsis: Jed MacKay's 2024 event featuring Blade — turned against Marvel's heroes — leading a vampire army that blots out the sun, forcing heroes to fight in an eternal night. A horror-flavored event building on MacKay's Avengers run.
author: Jed MacKay

subject: series
synopsis: Kenji Inoue and Kimitake Yoshioka's manga about scuba diving and extreme college socializing. Genuinely hilarious physical comedy and surprisingly effective emotional beats around diving.
author: Kenji Inoue

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Shooter and David Lapham's 1992 Valiant Harbinger: teenage psiot Peter Stanchek and his runaways rebel against Toyo Harada's Harbinger Foundation.

subject: series
synopsis: Kelly Thompson and Gurihiru's strip about Jeff the Land Shark — a baby land shark navigating everyday life. Pure joy in comics form.
author: Kelly Thompson

subject: series
synopsis: Kohei Horikoshi's blockbuster shonen follows Izuku Midoriya, born without powers in a world of superheroes, who inherits the greatest ability from the number-one hero and enrolls in a hero academy. Celebrated for its character work, escalating stakes, and loving deconstruction of superhero tropes.
author: Kohei Horikoshi

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's 2008 New Exiles: a reshuffled dimension-hopping team with Psylocke, Sage and Rogue, continuing Exiles for 18 issues.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Ryosuke Fuji's manga about a player who masters a terrible VR game then takes on the legendary top-tier game. Sharp commentary on gamer psychology and gaming culture with inventive virtual world-building.
author: Ryosuke Fuji

subject: series
synopsis: DC's legendary tryout anthology series that launched the Silver Age, debuting the Flash (Barry Allen), Green Lantern (Hal Jordan), Adam Strange, and Hawkman. Historically invaluable.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A tie-in limited series to the 2024 Absolute Power event, focusing on a task force assembled during the crisis involving the suppression of superhero powers.

subject: series
synopsis: Hiro Mashima's sequel to Fairy Tail, drawn by Atsuo Ueda: Natsu, Lucy and the team take on the guild's century-old unfinished quest.

subject: series
synopsis: Roy Thomas and Frank Robbins' 1975 World War II team of Captain America, Bucky, Namor and the original Human Torch, adding Union Jack and Spitfire.

subject: series
synopsis: J.M. DeMatteis and Shawn McManus's 1988 Doctor Fate, with Eric and Linda Strauss sharing the helmet, then William Messner-Loebs's Inza Nelson era.
author: J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor's digital-first prequel series to the Injustice fighting game, set in an alternate DC universe where a grief-maddened Superman becomes a global tyrant. Taylor's sharp dialogue and escalating moral stakes made this one of the best-regarded licensed tie-ins of the 2010s.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' anthology series reprinting golden-age western comics from the public domain — Bobby Benson, The Durango Kid, Ghost Rider (the cowboy original), and others — as part of the publisher's mission to preserve pre-superhero genre comics. A niche but valuable archive for enthusiasts of the golden age western genre.
author: Various (golden age reprints)

subject: series
synopsis: A collected edition of the landmark Milestone Comics series starring Curtis Metcalf, a.k.a. Hardware, a Black genius inventor who builds a power suit to wage war against his corrupt corporate sponsor.
author: Dwayne McDuffie

subject: series
synopsis: Chuck Dixon and John Romita Jr.'s 1992 Punisher: War Zone, Frank Castle undercover in the mob, later Larry Hama.

subject: series
synopsis: Nakaba Suzuki's fantasy about legendary knights who were framed for crimes they didn't commit. Fun shonen adventure with creative power systems and effective emotional beats.
author: Nakaba Suzuki

subject: series
synopsis: Recent Marvel event series pitting symbiote hosts against each other. Al Ewing's involvement ensures some intelligent symbiote mythology.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: Annual issues for The Amazing Spider-Man spanning multiple creative teams and decades, offering extended stories and character-defining moments outside the regular continuity of Marvel's flagship web-slinger title.
author: Eric Fein

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Michael Avon Oeming's police procedural set in a world of superheroes. Two homicide detectives investigate superhero-related deaths. Consistently sharp crime writing with genuine wit and emotional resonance.
author: Brian M. Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Peach Momoko writes and draws the 2024 Ultimate X-Men: Hisako Ichiki and other Tokyo teens discover mutant powers amid eerie supernatural horror.

subject: series
synopsis: Geoffrey Thorne's 2024 From the Ashes X-Force: Forge leads a global mutant rapid-response team.
author: Geoffrey Thorne

subject: series
synopsis: Yuzo Takada's manga about a trilobe — a three-eyed immortal being — and the human boy who becomes her undead servant. Gothic fantasy adventure with an unusual protagonist dynamic.
author: Yuzo Takada

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak and Jae Lee's 2013 Batman/Superman: the New 52 heroes' first meeting and multiversal team-ups, later Peter Tomasi.

subject: series
synopsis: Fawcett's Billy Batson stories are among the finest golden-age superhero works — playful, imaginative, and with a genuine heart. Otto Binder's writing and CC Beck's art create a unique charm.
author: Otto Binder

subject: series
synopsis: Seth's self-reflective anthology series from Drawn & Quarterly that collected his major works including It's a Good Life If You Don't Weaken and Clyde Fans, known for its nostalgic aesthetics and meditative pacing.
author: Seth

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's digital Star Wars webcomics published online, featuring shorter episodic Star Wars adventures in a digital-first format. Part of Marvel's efforts to expand Star Wars comics content across platforms.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Long-running DC series pairing the World's Finest heroes in adventures that play up their contrasting personalities and complementary abilities. Launched by Jeph Loeb and Ed McGuinness with the celebrated 'Public Enemies' arc, the series became a showcase for major creative teams and bold visual storytelling across its 87-issue run.
author: Jeph Loeb

subject: series
synopsis: Looseboy's psychological thriller manga about a girl who appears to be a normal student at a school for superpowered people — but has a lethal secret agenda. Smart, dark, and full of effective twists.
author: Looseboy

subject: series
synopsis: François Froideval's French dark-fantasy saga, painted first by Olivier Ledroit: the half-elf mercenary Wismerhill rises amid wars between the Empire and the cult of the Black Moon.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1983 ongoing series spinning out of Green Lantern and New Teen Titans, following the alien rebel team fighting the Citadel empire across the Vegan star system. Notable early work from the Marv Wolfman team.
author: Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: Denny O'Neil and Denys Cowan's 1986 The Question: Vic Sage trains in martial arts and Zen and fights corruption in Hub City.
author: Dennis O'Neil

subject: series
synopsis: Marv Wolfman's 1983 Vigilante: Judge Adrian Chase turns vigilante against the mob, a dark, violent run with an Alan Moore two-parter.
author: Paul Kupperberg, Marv Wolfman

subject: series
synopsis: Wildcats volume 2 (1999-2001): Lobdell and Travis Charest's relaunch, then Joe Casey and Sean Phillips' corporate-espionage run leading into Wildcats 3.0.

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Zub and Roberto De La Torre's 2023 Titan Comics relaunch of Robert E. Howard's Conan, faithful sword-and-sorcery adventures.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2024 summer event in which Amanda Waller strips the DC Universe's heroes of their powers using stolen technology.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Marv Wolfman's 1991 Deathstroke the Terminator: Slade Wilson as mercenary anti-hero, spun out of the New Teen Titans.
author: Marv Wolfman, Dale Hrebik

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor's digital prequel to the fighting game: after the Joker tricks him into killing Lois, Superman seizes control of Earth and the heroes split.

subject: series
synopsis: The companion series to Justice League America following a European branch of the team — Captain Atom, Metamorpho, Flash, Power Girl — with Giffen and DeMatteis's signature humor transplanted across the Atlantic. Less celebrated than its sibling but consistently entertaining.
author: Keith Giffen, J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Parker's acclaimed all-ages Avengers series featuring Iron Man, Captain America, Giant-Girl, Hulk, Storm, and Wolverine in self-contained adventures. Praised by readers of all ages for its wit, character warmth, and ability to be genuinely entertaining without relying on continuity — often cited as one of Marvel's best all-ages titles of its era.
author: Jeff Parker

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's promotional magazine covering upcoming releases and behind-the-scenes content. A historical document of 1980s Marvel more than a comics narrative.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Tom DeFalco's long-running MC2 universe series about Mayday Parker, daughter of Peter and MJ. Charming legacy hero work with strong family themes; Salicrup's editing ensured consistent quality for 100+ issues.
author: Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: The original golden age Namor series by Bill Everett. The defining early Namor stories — brooding, anti-heroic, and magnificently drawn by Everett.
author: Bill Everett

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Silver Age sci-fi/horror anthology running from 1956–1968, mixing alien encounters with twist-ending mystery tales typical of the era.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning's Legion of Super-Heroes run. DnA bring their cosmic sensibility to the 30th century with good results.
author: Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Mark Bagley's reinvention of Spider-Man's origin for the modern era, treating high school, relationships, and identity with unprecedented depth. The gold standard of Ultimate Marvel and one of the most accessible long-running superhero comics.
author: Brian M. Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Rick Remender's 2012 Uncanny Avengers: Captain America's Unity Squad of Avengers and X-Men against the Red Skull and the Apocalypse Twins.
author: Rick Remender

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman's new Skybound series that reintroduced the Transformers/G.I. Joe universe. A promising sci-fi action premise with Kirkman's characteristic character work.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: Stephanie Phillips' 2024 Phoenix: Jean Grey as the cosmic Phoenix, guarding the universe apart from the X-Men.
author: Stephanie Phillips

subject: series
synopsis: Saladin Ahmed and Martín Cóccolo's 2024 From the Ashes Wolverine: Logan alone against new threats after Krakoa.
author: Saladin Ahmed

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David's 1996 Supergirl: the Matrix merges with Linda Danvers to become an Earth-born Angel, a spiritual cult favorite drawn by Gary Frank and Leonard Kirk.
author: Peter David

subject: series
synopsis: Kara Zor-El's New 52 series (2011-2015): Michael Green, Mike Johnson and Mahmud Asrar's newly arrived Kryptonian, later the Red Lantern arc.

subject: series
synopsis: Comprehensive omnibus edition collecting Nick Spencer's acclaimed Amazing Spider-Man run.
author: Nick Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's Angel: After the Fall, the canonical sequel to the TV series plotted with Joss Whedon — Los Angeles sent to hell — followed by Bill Willingham's run.
author: Joss Whedon, Kelley Armstrong

subject: series
synopsis: Jeph Loeb and Jim Lee's blockbuster arc introducing the villain Hush, featuring virtually every major Bat-villain and a mystery about a childhood friend. One of the best-selling Batman arcs of the 2000s.
author: Jeph Loeb

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Abnett's digital tie-in to the Infinite Crisis MOBA game: heroes and villains from DC's alternate Earths battle a multiversal threat.

subject: series
synopsis: A UN-sanctioned splinter Justice League. Christopher Priest's run introduced Triumph; the series struggled to define its own identity.
author: Dennis Hopeless

subject: series
synopsis: Rumiko Takahashi's beloved martial arts romantic comedy follows Ranma Saotome, who transforms into a girl when splashed with cold water due to a training accident in cursed springs. A cornerstone of 1990s manga culture known for its enormous cast, endless romantic complications, and inventive martial arts parodies.
author: Rumiko Takahashi

subject: series
synopsis: Gregory Wright's Marvel series about the mercenary queen of Symkaria. Competent international action-adventure; an underused character who deserved better.
author: Gregory Wright

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Crumb's revolutionary underground anthology launched in 1968 on the streets of San Francisco; the founding document of underground comix, featuring Crumb alongside S. Clay Wilson, Gilbert Shelton, and other countercultural cartoonists.
author: Robert Crumb

subject: series
synopsis: Modern Doctor Strange series balancing action, magic, and character depth.

subject: series
synopsis: Hawkman volume 3 (1993-1996), Katar Hol's post-Zero Hour series; our files also hold Geoff Johns and James Robinson's 2002 Hawkman.
author: William Messner-Loebs

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Ware's formally inventive one-man anthology, where Jimmy Corrigan and Rusty Brown began, in intricate, melancholy design.

subject: series
synopsis: Craig Kyle and Christopher Yost's 2008 X-Force: Cyclops's secret mutant kill squad led by Wolverine, into Messiah War and Second Coming.

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Williamson and Tom Reilly's 2024 Energon Universe G.I. Joe from Skybound: Duke and the Joes rebuilt to fight Cobra alongside the Transformers.

subject: series
synopsis: Wildstorm's 2007 Midnighter: Garth Ennis opens with a time-travel hit on Hitler, followed by Keith Giffen and guest writers including Brian K. Vaughan.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse Presents relaunched as an 80-page monthly anthology (2011-2014), with new Concrete stories alongside dozens of shorts.

subject: series
synopsis: Gail Simone and Talent Caldwell's 2006 Gen 13 reboot: teens with no memories discover their powers inside the government program Tabula Rasa.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Cornell's 2014 Wolverine: a powerless, armored Logan goes undercover with a crime boss ahead of Death of Wolverine.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Tobin and Colleen Coover's companion anthology to the Eisner-winning Bandette, collecting stories that expand the colorful world of Paris's most charming thief — including tales of her network of young street informants and allies. Retains all the warmth and wit of the main series with a broader cast spotlight.
author: Paul Tobin

subject: series
synopsis: Kanehito Yamada and Tsukasa Abe's bittersweet fantasy follows the elven mage Frieren long after her hero party defeated the Demon King, as she grapples with outliving her human companions and the weight of time. A meditative masterwork on grief, memory, and what makes a life meaningful.
author: Kanehito Yamada

subject: series
synopsis: Hiroya Oku's ultraviolent sci-fi manga about dead people forced into alien-hunting games. Relentlessly bleak and often gratuitous; the alien designs are genuinely remarkable and some character work lands.
author: Hiroya Oku

subject: series
synopsis: Judd Winick's biweekly series following Captain Atom, Fire, Ice, Booster Gold, and Blue Beetle as they hunt a mind-wiped Maxwell Lord, a well-regarded character study of the classic JLI team.
author: Judd Winick

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's comic series continuing the adventures of Ahsoka Tano — former Padawan of Anakin Skywalker and fan favorite since The Clone Wars — bridging gaps in her story and expanding on her appearances in the Disney+ live-action era. Aimed at existing fans of the character rather than new readers.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Barbara Kesel and Bart Sears' CrossGen book about the godlike First, two rival houses whose politics loom above the Sigil-bearers' worlds.

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman's run on the Ultimate Ultimates, featuring grand-scale threats including the Children of Tomorrow and a restructured take on the team following the Divided We Fall crossover.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Second edition saga collections of Usagi Yojimbo reprinting the classic adventures in new formats.
author: Stan Sakai

subject: series
synopsis: Takehiko Inoue's stunning manga adaptation of Eiji Yoshikawa's novel about the legendary swordsman Miyamoto Musashi, following his journey from a violent youth to enlightenment. Renowned for its breathtaking ink-brush artwork and meditative depth.
author: Takehiko Inoue

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns' 2022 Justice Society of America, launched from The New Golden Age: Helena Wayne's Huntress and a time-lost JSA against an enemy erasing heroes.

subject: series
synopsis: Kara Zor-El's 2005 series: Jeph Loeb and Michael Turner's reintroduction, uneven years, then Sterling Gates and Jamal Igle's acclaimed run.
author: Sterling Gates, James Peaty

subject: series
synopsis: Arnold Drake and Bruno Premiani's original Doom Patrol (1963-1968): the Chief's misfit heroes Robotman, Negative Man and Elasti-Girl, ending in their famous sacrifice.

subject: series
synopsis: Hirohiko Araki's eighth JoJo's Bizarre Adventure part: in an alternate Morioh, the amnesiac Josuke Higashikata uncovers the Higashikata family's secrets and the Rokakaka fruit.
